title: What Are the Ants Doing with That Flower?

collection.credit: NEW EVENTS — WHAT'S THAT DOING HERE? (WD-01 to WD-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)

ledger.why: the casting line (the roles carry it)

collection.description: A line of ants marches through a villager's hut carrying a whole red flower like a festival float.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A long line of ants is marching through (name1)'s hut, in at the door and out through a gap in the wall. That's not so unusual. What is unusual is that in the middle of the line, carried along on dozens of tiny backs, is a whole red flower, much bigger than all of them, bobbing along like a festival float.

a.name: Answer A
a.text: (name1) follows the line outside, round the back of the hut, and across the path to a little mound of earth where the flower, after a great deal of effort, disappears into the ground, petal by petal. (name1) sits back on (his/her) heels. (He/She) has never wondered what ants do with flowers. Now (he/she) can't stop wondering.

text_only.reason: the word's everyday sense (a thing, a sound or a worry disappears); nobody goes missing

b.name: Answer B
b.text: (name1) opens the door as wide as it will go, and moves the water jar, so the ants have a clear road. The flower passes through without a hitch. (name1) feels oddly helpful, like a road builder for very small people. Later (he/she) finds a single red petal left behind on the floor, and keeps it.
